journal.author: Claude
journal.text:
Plan update: what decides Zeus runs, and two faster drills
Every ranked Zeus run (about 140) plus the Zeus Close and Zeus Far drills was split into parts by what the bot is doing: just turned, catching up, settled in a strafe, walking toward or away, respawning.
What it showed: the first 0.15 s after the bot turns is the weakest moment (on the bot only 10–15% of the time), but it's reaction time and good and bad runs are equally weak there. What separates good runs from bad is the settled strafe: once caught up, staying on the bot at its speed. That's about 68 points between the top and bottom quarter of runs, with catching up adding 12. When off the bot, the aim is behind it more than 9 times in 10, not past it.
Changes: SCX Close Strafes is out of ZEUS FOCUS (a different bot; a warm-up doesn't carry over) and two Zeus Close 0.85X runs open the session instead. New Zeus Far 115% and Zeus Close 115% use the Zeus bot with its own time scale at 1.15: in test runs it moved 15% faster (600 to about 695) and turned 15% quicker (212 to 182 ms), with the same strafe rhythm. Three runs of each come right before their normal versions. Ranked stays at 8.
So far: ranked Zeus typical score 489 before Oct 17, 502 since (62 runs). Small and early.
One thing to try: catch up, then glide. After each turn get back on, then lock onto the bot's speed and keep the hand moving at that one pace until the next turn.

journal.author: Claude
journal.text:
Playlist change: a slow-turn block before Zeus, and two drills dropped
What changed: ZEUS WEAKNESS is now 15 runs. It opens with 8 slow-turn runs (Controlsphere OW, Mixed XYZ Strafes Slow Accel, Reactive Adjustments Strafes and Slow Accel 'STT' Short, 2 each), then SCX Close Strafes 3, Thin Fast 2 and Far BZN 2. Pennytracking and Closely Strafing Kytan are out. RANK INT B is now 32 runs: 6 slow-turn runs in Normal mode (Controlsphere OW, Air Easy Invincible 4, Mixed XYZ Strafes Slow Accel) sit right before the 8 ranked Zeus runs. Ranked Zeus is still 8 per sitting.
Why: over-aim on ranked Zeus has been 34–39% of corrections on every recorded day since Oct 8, even with the "land short" cue. On Pennytracking and Kytan, about 2 in 3 corrections went past the bot. Those drills were teaching the snap-back, even while their scores rose.
How to play the block: no hurry and no score-chasing. After each turn, let the bot come to you, then make one short, smooth correction onto its near edge. Use a small burst from the wrist or fingers, then let go. Lower scores here are fine. If you hit well under half your shots, swap in an easier version. On ranked Zeus, one cue: trust the strafe, land short.
What to watch: ranked Zeus over-aim (about 36% now). Working means about 32% or lower over a week. Score comes after that and may dip at first. If over-aim hasn't moved by about Nov 5, the next test is drills at a different sensitivity.

journal.author: Claude
journal.text:
Goal change: Zeus Track first
The end goal is the same: Master 3 on all 6 Intermediate ranked tracking scenarios. What changed is the main focus. From Oct 16 the plan pushes the weakest of the six, Zeus Track, with about 80% of practice time, and the other five keep a short daily block so they still move.
Why Zeus: it's the furthest behind for the work put in. Its typical score has sat at 486–498 for 7 weeks over 516 ranked runs, and its best (591) is from early September. Master 3 is 726. The other five rose or held on about a third of the practice.
How the 80% is spent: not on more ranked Zeus. Days with 17+ ranked Zeus runs scored no better than days with 1–8 (490 against 500). The time goes to the habit that separates good Zeus runs from bad ones: over-aim after turns (34% of corrections on good runs, 41% on bad, stuck at 34–39% every day).
New daily order: ZEUS DAILY (Zeus-distance drills, Zeus EZ Burst, the slow-turn block, then 8 ranked Zeus), then one OTHERS playlist (two of the other five, 5 runs each, rotating 1, 2, 3). ZEUS SECOND (3 slow-turn runs and 8 ranked Zeus) is optional a few hours later, and logged separately to test whether spaced sittings help.
Check around Nov 5: ranked Zeus over-aim clearly below 34%, and the other five not dropping more than about 3%. If over-aim hasn't moved, the next trial is more ranked Zeus in spaced sittings.

journal.author: Claude
journal.text:
Playlist: RANK INT B (26 runs, 08:51–09:49)
What happened: Your best B day so far on PASU XYZ: a median of 486 (baseline 472) and a best of 532. Zeus held at its usual level, 498 (baseline 491), and PASU 0.85x sat right on its baseline, 335 (340), with a best of 385.
Conditions: The cold start is still there despite the two PASU 0.6x warm-up runs (430 and 440). PASU 0.85x opened 302, 302, then climbed into the 330s and 385. PASU XYZ opened 398 and 434, then 516, 532 and 522. So in both PASU scenarios the first two runs are the low ones, the same pattern as Oct 8. You didn't do the R5Reloaded warm-up today, and you'd been up a few hours already, so being awake longer didn't remove the cold start on its own. Yesterday's A day had both (R5Reloaded first, not straight after waking) and no cold start, which points at the R5Reloaded warm-up rather than time awake. Two days isn't proof, though.
Rest: The median rest was 69 s, the longest yet, in the range that has scored better so far. 44 restarts, though, the most of any day. If most were early quits on bad starts, they don't hurt, but they do add time.
Aim recorder: Zeus over-aim stayed at about 4 in 10 corrections, the same as Oct 8, and far-away points are still the weakest (about 7 a second, against 8–9 up close). PASU XYZ's best runs (516–532) had over-aim at 3 in 10 or less. The 398 opener was at 5 in 10.
Next time: The B playlist now opens with 2 relaxed Normal-mode runs of PASU 0.85x itself instead of 0.6x. They don't count toward ranked. On the next B day, see whether the first ranked PASU runs still start low.

Playlist: Extra practice outside the plan: Air Track Smooth V3 Advanced (ranked, 10:23), Zeus visualisation video, and ANY STRAFES - HS from the 143 GROUND BENCHMARK routine (19:32)
What happened: Air Track Advanced scored 312 (your best there is 330). You were on the ball 26% of the time. Keeping up wasn't the problem: you didn't trail the ball. The points went on over-aim, about 101 times a minute, and on shake while on the ball, which slid you off it. Your middle 20 seconds were the weakest part of the run (19% on the ball, against 25% at the start and 34% at the end). Any Strafes scored 705 at 25% accuracy (it only counts headshots).
How I measured it: The aim recorder logged the run, and time on the ball was matched to the game's own accuracy. Videos made for watching: your run 20% better (378), and a 20% better version of your best recorded Zeus this week (537 on Oct 8, shown at 643) to practise visualising.
Conditions: Two plan changes today. The RANK INT B warm-up is now 2 Normal-mode runs of PASU 0.85x instead of 0.6x, because the cold start kept happening. The aim recorder's phase 7 is live: it fills its bot slots with moving bots first, records clicking runs 120 times a second, and sees the real height of flying bots.
Next time: Over-aim is the same thing that separated your best runs on Zeus, PASU XYZ and Sphere S. On tomorrow's A day, on Air Track, make smaller corrections and settle on the ball, and keep it up through the middle of the run, where today's run dropped.

journal.author: Claude
journal.text:

What happened: All three scenarios held their usual level. PASU 0.85x median 335 (best 377), the same as this morning. PASU XYZ 467 (best 514), a little under this morning's 486 and close to its baseline of 472. Zeus 492 (best 523), on its baseline of 491.

The first ranked 0.85x runs were 316 and 334, against 302 and 302 this morning, and PASU XYZ opened at 484 instead of 398. A 27-minute break came partway through PASU 0.85x, and the runs after it (336, 349, 335, 319, 377) were slightly better than the ones before.

journal.author: Claude
journal.text:
Playlist change: Zeus Weakness replaces Zeus Builder as the A-day Zeus playlist
What changed: A new 17-run playlist, Zeus Weakness, now takes Zeus Builder's place on A days, in the in-game plan banner and on this site. It starts with 1 run of Zeus Track Evo - Noblink (EZ). Most runs go to close-range drills: SCX Close Strafes 3, Pennytracking 3, Thin Fast 2, Closely Strafing Kytan 1. Then Slow Accel 'STT' Short 2 for mid distance, Zeus Track Far BZN Edition 2 for the far start of each round, and 3 ranked Zeus Track runs to finish. Zeus Builder isn't deleted and can come back any time.
Why: Zeus is your main focus because it's your weakest ranked tracking scenario, so its playlist should train only the parts of Zeus where you lose points. The aim recorder's 21 ranked Zeus runs (Oct 8 and 10) show where those are:
- The moment the bot changes direction. About 8 in 10 of your off-target moments are on the side the bot just left: late, or still moving the old way.
- Over-aim after those turns. About 4 in 10 corrections go through the bot, the same far, mid and close.
- The close part of each round, about half of every run. Your best runs score well over a point a second more there than your worst. The far start is your lowest-scoring part, but it's about the same on good and bad runs, so it gets fewer runs.
- Not problems: reaction (about 130 ms every run), up-down aim, and losing the bot for long stretches.
What was kept and dropped: Five Zeus Builder drills stay because they train those turns: Zeus EZ, Kytan, Pennytracking, Thin Fast and Slow Accel 'STT' Short. Three are dropped because they train slow tracking, floating jumps and target switching, which the data says aren't Zeus problems: Ground Plaza FS No UFO, Controlsphere OW Test and TAMTargetSwitch Smooth Easy VSB. Two are new: SCX Close Strafes, for turns at Zeus's exact close distance, and Zeus Track Far BZN Edition, for the far start on its own. Each drill's run count matches how many points its weak spot costs.
Next time: The two new drills will climb at first just from learning them, so the test is Zeus Track's own median, not the drill scores. On every drill, after each turn, make a smaller correction and land on the near edge of the bot. Being slightly behind costs less than going through it.

journal.author: Claude
journal.text:
Playlist: ZEUS WEAKNESS, first play (17 runs, 22:18–23:08), plus 1 run of ZEUS WEAKNESS 3 (23:12)
What happened: This is the new Zeus playlist you made today. It now replaces ZEUS BUILDER as the A-day Zeus playlist, at your request. It's built around where Zeus loses the most time: just after the bot changes direction, when about 8 in 10 off-target moments have the crosshair on the side the bot just left. The far, small bot at the start of each round comes second. Slow Accel 'STT' Short scored 352, a new best (old best 301). The two new drills set their starting marks: SCX Close Strafes 580, 571, 584, then 648 in ZEUS WEAKNESS 3, and FAR BZN 1012 and 1108. Kytan held at 497 and Pennytracking was 540, 565 and 525. Thin Fast was your lowest yet, 1175 and 1265 (usually 1350–1650).
Conditions: This was your third session of the day and it ran past 23:00. The three ranked Zeus runs at the end, 488, 409 and 432, were the day's lowest (the evening's median was 492). Over-aim in the two low ones was about 45%, against about 1 in 3 on the 488. The game crashed twice just before this session (21:50 and 21:56). No runs were lost, but it added to a late start.
Aim recorder: A Zeus "teacher" video now marks three of these weaknesses on tonight's runs (videos/zeus_teacher/).
Next time: On Zeus, as soon as the bot changes direction, go with it to its new side instead of finishing the old movement.

journal.author: Ryan
journal.text: Played my first Aimbeast session of the day. It was pretty good, and it felt like I was slowly returning to baseline. I got a new personal best on Air Control, which I didn't expect. One difference: I didn't play as soon as I woke up. After waking, I played imported versions of all the Aimbeast ranked V1 tracking scenarios in R5Reloaded, the aim trainer, and then a couple of rounds of ranked. I felt like that warmed me up for Aimbeast, but I don't know if that's actually true. It's correlation, not causation. I'm going to take a bit of a break before my next session.

journal.author: Claude
journal.text:
Playlist: RANK INT A (26 runs including the 2 warm-up runs, 07:05–08:16)
What happened: Your best A day so far. All three medians beat their pre-plan baselines: Smooth Thin 438 (baseline 429), Air Track 482 (447), Sphere S 740 (663). Sphere S hit 853, your best since the score log started on Sep 23 (old best there 842). Your all-time best is still 878, and Master 3 is 880. On the Oct 7 morning these medians were 375, 360 and 557.
Aim recorder: In Sphere S and Smooth Thin, your best run was the one where you swung past the bot least. The 853 Sphere S run went past it on 1 in 4 corrections, against 1 in 3 to 2 in 5 on the other runs. The 473 Smooth Thin run was 1 in 5, against about 1 in 3. Air Track didn't follow the pattern (its 526 swung past as often as the rest). (Fix: Air Track and Sphere S were wrongly skipped at first because bots left over from earlier scenarios stand still in the level. The script now ignores bots that never move.)
Conditions: Unlike Oct 7 and Oct 8, you didn't play straight after waking. You warmed up first in R5Reloaded with all the Aimbeast ranked V1 tracking scenarios plus a couple of rounds of ranked, then did the Air Control Sphere warm-up (910 and 912). This is the first A day with that much warm-up, and the first with no cold start: Smooth Thin's first counted run was 449, not its usual low opener. As you said, one day can't separate the warm-up from just being further from waking, but it's worth repeating.
Rest: The median rest was 57 s, in the longer range that has scored better so far. One 13-minute break came mid-Sphere S, and the runs after it (726, 746) sat on the day's median, so the break didn't hurt.
Next time: Repeat the same order (wake, R5Reloaded warm-up, then the playlist) on B tomorrow and note it, so we can see whether PASU 0.85x loses its cold start too. In-game, aim to stop on the bot after a correction instead of swinging through it. That separated your best runs today.

journal.author: Claude
journal.text:
Playlist: ZEUS BUILDER, first play of the new version (16 runs, 09:52–11:06), plus test runs for the recorder (11:07–12:16)
What happened: Two drill bests. Pennytracking 630 (old best 575) and Thin Fast 1650 (old best 1565). The other repeat drills held steady against Oct 8: Slow Accel 289 (294), Kytan 485 (484), and Ground Plaza slipped a little to 342 (355). The two new left-right and over-aim drills set their starting marks: Controlsphere OW 6422 and 6804, and TAMTargetSwitch 31 and 32 kills.
Conditions: Played 95 minutes after finishing RANK INT A, with one 17-minute break mid-playlist. The runs after 11:07 (1 Wall 4 Targets, Star Clicking, Popcorn, PASU XYZ, a Sphere and a Zeus EZ run) were tests of the recorder, not practice, so they aren't judged here.
How I measured it: The recorder was upgraded today, and this is the first data with the changes.
- It now sees the real height of flying bots. In Sphere S and Air Track the game moves the ball's body, not the bot itself.
- It fills its 8 bot slots with moving bots first. Leftover bots from earlier scenarios were taking slots, and TAMTargetSwitch went from 10 of 27 kills caught to 30 of 30.
- Clicking runs switch to 120 snapshots a second.
- It costs about 0.07 ms per frame on tracking, so no FPS loss.
Next time: Keep the new version as it is until the Oct 25 check-in. Today counts as its first data point.

Only PASU 0.85x, the first scenario, was low, and it climbed from 265 to 354, a cold start rather than a slump (its last three days were 346, 328 and 350). What happened: Every repeat drill went up on yesterday: Ground Plaza 355 (best 387, above its old best of 369), 'STT' Short 0.5x 240 (184), Slow Accel 294 (263), Kytan 484 (478), Smooth Thin S 164 (142), Thin Fast 1458 (best 1565). First plays of the new Pennytracking drill: 500, then 575. The extra Zeus runs held at a median of 502, the same as before the builder.
Conditions: Played straight after RANK INT B, still within the first 90 minutes after waking, so it was a 90-minute, 42-run morning with short breaks. No sign of fatigue: almost every drill's second run was equal or better.
Next time: Most of today's gains are from learning the new drills, so they aren't skill changes yet. Zeus Track itself didn't move straight after the builder, which is normal; any carry-over will show over days. Write a one-line note on sleep, screen and sound before you play.

journal.author: Claude
journal.text:
Playlist: Video check of this morning's 12 Zeus Track runs (from the Twitch VOD)
How I measured it: I downloaded the Zeus part of the stream (06:10–07:00, 1600×900 at 60 fps) and matched each run to the practice log using the clock on screen. I then read 30 frames a second from every run, about 1,700 per run. On each frame a script finds the cyan target by its colour and measures how far it is from the crosshair at the centre of the screen, left-right and up-down, scaled to the target's size. A frame counts as on target when the crosshair is inside the target's outline. A miss counts when the crosshair is outside for at least 0.1 s. A miss is up-down when the vertical distance is larger, and left-right otherwise. An overshoot is a miss on the opposite side within 0.2 s of the previous one, meaning the crosshair passed through the target. To check it works, time on target matched the scores with a correlation of 0.84. About 4 seconds of each run were left out because the target was too small to detect. (Corrected: I first thought the target was missing. Zeus actually has three rounds of about 20 seconds, and each one starts with the bot far away straight ahead, so it's tiny on screen.) Limits: one session of 12 runs, and the video can't show grip or hand tension.
What happened: I measured the crosshair against the target on every frame. Time on target was 31–38% per run, and it matched the scores closely: the three lowest-scoring runs (453, 455, 472) were the three lowest on target. About 95% of the time off target was left-right misses. Only about 5% came from the up/down kicks, although runs with more kick misses did score lower. Almost half the misses (47%) were overshoots: the crosshair went through the target to the other side right after a correction. Each run had 9–16 long misses of half a second or more, and those decided which runs scored well.
Conditions: The scores show no fatigue. Time on target was the same in the first and last 20 seconds of runs, and the same before and after ZEUS BUILDER.
Next time: On Zeus, aim to under-correct after a direction change. Land on the near edge of the target instead of swinging through it, and accept being slightly behind rather than past it. The left-right direction changes are where most of the points are, more than the kicks.

journal.author: Claude
journal.text:
Playlist: Zeus Track, 5 extra ranked runs (10:42–10:51), first runs measured by the new aim recorder
What happened: Scores 469, 537, 476, 514, 514. Time on target was 31%, 39%, 34%, 38%, 34%, so the 537 run was the best on target. About 4 in 10 corrections went past the bot in every run (31–40%). By distance, I score least when the bot is far away at the start of each round (7.2 points a second), most in the middle (9.3) and a bit less up close (8.6). Reaction to direction changes stayed at about 130 ms. (Corrected: earlier numbers here measured the bot's size in degrees, which made it look easier to stay on when it was far away. Now its real size at its real distance is used, and time on target matches the scores more closely.)
How I measured it: A read-only game mod records your aim and the bot's position 60 times a second during each run. It costs about 0.04 ms per frame, so no FPS loss. A script then works out time on target, how quickly you follow direction changes, and how often a correction goes past the bot.
Next time: Keep landing on the near edge of the bot after a direction change rather than swinging through it, and pay extra attention at the start of each round when the bot is far away and small. Your reactions are already quick, so the gains are in the size of the correction, not its speed.

journal.author: Claude
journal.text:
What happened: First session of the plan, RANK INT A, all 24 runs. Medians were well under your baseline: Smooth Thin 375 (baseline 429), Air Track 150% 360 (447), Sphere S 557 (663).
Conditions: Played within 10 minutes of waking, f.lux on, a dimmed screen, no sound, hitmarker on then off for the last 4 runs. Five changes at once, so this session says little about your skill.
Rest: A first look at rest across all 97 runs from Oct 6 and 7. The first attempt on each scenario scores about 3% below its usual, and the first run after a 15+ minute break about 6% below. That's warm-up, not tiredness. Inside a scenario, runs after 20 s to 2 min of rest scored about 2% higher than runs started within 20 s, but that's too little data to trust yet. Time of day shows no pattern. Treat the first run on each scenario as warm-up and don't judge yourself on it.
Next time: Change one thing at a time. Keep no sound if that's the goal, but play fully awake with normal brightness so the next sessions are comparable.

journal.author: Ryan

journal.author: Claude
journal.text:
Playlist: RANK INT A, second time today (24 runs, 20:27–21:34)
What happened: Much better than this morning. Medians: Smooth Thin 418 (morning 375), Air Track 481 (360), Sphere S 706 (557). Air Track and Sphere S beat their pre-plan baselines (447 and 663), and Smooth Thin was just under (429). Best runs: 464, 537 and 780.
Conditions: Evening, wide awake, about 15 hours after the morning's just-woke-up session. No note on screen, sound or hitmarker, so the exact differences aren't known.
Rest: Ryan lengthened his rests on purpose after reading the rest table. His median rest between runs of the same scenario went from 16 s this morning to 54 s. Across all 121 runs so far, rests of 20 s to 2 min score about 3% above rests under 20 s, so it's worth keeping. Tonight's jump was 11–34%, though, and within the session longer-rest runs weren't clearly better. Most of the gain came from playing awake with normal settings.
Next time: Keep whatever you did tonight, and write it down so it can be repeated. The morning was conditions, not skill. The first run of each scenario was again the lowest, so keep treating it as warm-up.

aim_moments.focus: Ease into the bot and match its speed. No hard stops, no over-aiming.

moments.title: Over-aim: Zeus Track
moments.text: The bot keeps moving the same way, but my correction is so fast it goes straight through it and out the other side. Then I have to correct back.

moments.title: Catch up, then brake
moments.text: The bot gets away, I make a big catch-up, then I nearly stop dead while the bot keeps going. Watch my aim-speed bar empty out.

moments.title: Stop-go instead of smooth
moments.text: Even when I'm on the bot, my aim speed pulses: too fast, then too slow, about three times a second. The smooth version just matches the bot's speed.

moments.title: Over-aim: Sphere S
moments.text: The bot keeps going the same way, and my catch-up goes through it and out the other side. This scenario only shows left-right: the recorder can't see the bot's real height here.

moments.title: Over-aim: Air Track
moments.text: Same habit on a flying bot: a fast correction that doesn't brake in time, then a correction back. Left-right only, for the same reason as Sphere S.

moments.title: Over-aim: Smooth Thin
moments.text: I'm close, speed up to close the gap, and end up on the far side of a thin bot. The smooth version eases in and just matches its speed.
